reason: I'd install the open-source version the week it hits Hacker News and play with it on our internal repos, but I can't pay $99 a month for something I can't point at client code. Half our clients haven't signed off on AI agents touching their repos at all, let alone unattended overnight.
objection: Our clients may not allow AI agents on their code, and a pre-alpha tool built by one developer running agents overnight with nobody watching is a hard sell to them and to my boss.
would_change_my_mind: A client contract or policy template that clearly allows this, plus proof it runs stably on real projects for a few months, so I can actually use it on billable work.
